significance.justification: Verified true, the claim would establish that a source-plus-relation, target-blind retrieval key causally governs relational recall, while “key-distance predicts per-example reverse-recall failure”; this combines a form-(ii) mechanism with a form-(iii) predictive coupling that fixes expected outcomes for reverse and paraphrased queries rather than merely locating stored facts. It would establish both a behavioral phenomenon and a mechanistic explanation, connecting the reversal behavior documented by Berglund et al. (2023) to a specific read-side addressing failure and extending factual-recall decompositions such as Geva et al. (2023) into predictions about when extraction succeeds. A verified-false result would informatively rule out source/relation key mismatch as a common explanation of reversal and paraphrase failures, although qualifiers such as “almost entirely” and “largely blind” slightly weaken determinacy; true and false nevertheless denote distinguishable architectures of retrieval. Topic substitution leaves only the generic question of query-dependent knowledge access, which would not earn this score—the specific target-blind structure, causal consequence, and key-distance law are what place it above the topic median.

reach.justification: The named handles are “key-distance,” an internal predictor of reverse-recall failure, and the “key-alignment” intervention that maps a reverse query toward the stored forward key. Key-distance is ex ante because it can flag a likely failure from the query representation before answer generation, while key-alignment supplies an inference-time action window; however, the claim concedes that alignment requires “knowing the target’s forward fact,” sharply limiting production use. After per-model re-extraction, the substantive prediction still travels as a relation—greater distance from the stored forward key predicts retrieval failure—rather than merely as a procedure for finding an unrelated direction, and the hypothesis covers reverse and paraphrased queries across relational fact types rather than one dataset. Likely downstream users include retrieval-mechanism researchers and model auditors, but not broad deployment practitioners without a way to obtain the forward key; deleting the key-distance relation and intervention leaves only the topic and would not justify this above-median reach.
